## Orbital space travelers
### European Space Agency members
[edit]
Some of these astronauts participated in national space programme activity unrelated to their home country's contemporary or subsequent membership of the European Space Agency.
*   Franz Viehböck, first Austrian in space. — Soyuz TM-13/12 (1991)

*   Dirk Frimout, first Belgian in space. — STS-45 (1992)  
*   Frank De Winne, EAC — Soyuz TMA-1/TM-34 (2002), Soyuz TMA-15 (2009)

*   Andreas Mogensen, EAC, first Dane in space. — Soyuz TMA-18M (2015)/16M (2015), SpaceX Crew-7 (2023)

## Orbital space travelers
### European Space Agency members
*   Jean-Loup Chrétien, CNES (Intercosmos), first French person in space and first non-Soviet European to walk in space — Soyuz T-6 (1982), Soyuz TM-7/6 (1988), STS-86 (1997)  
*   Patrick Baudry, second Frenchman in space, born in Douala, Cameroon — STS-51-G (1985)  
*   Michel Tognini, EAC — Soyuz TM-15/14 (1992), STS-93 (1999)  
*   Jean-Pierre Haigneré, EAC — Soyuz TM-17/16 (1993), Soyuz TM-29 (1999)  
*   Jean-François Clervoy, EAC — STS-66 (1994), STS-84 (1997), STS-103 (1999)  
*   Jean-Jacques Favier, born in Kehl, Germany — STS-78 (1996)  
*   Claudie André-Deshays Haigneré, EAC, first Frenchwoman in space (Mir, 1996) — Soyuz TM-24/23 (1996), Soyuz TM-33/32 (2001)  
*   Léopold Eyharts, EAC — Soyuz TM-27/26 (1998), STS-122/123 (2008)  
*   Philippe Perrin, EAC, born in Meknes, Morocco — STS-111 (2002)  
*   Thomas Pesquet, EAC — Soyuz MS-03 (2016), SpaceX Crew-2 (2021)  
*   Sophie Adenot, EAC — SpaceX Crew-12 (2026)

## Orbital space travelers
### European Space Agency members
*   Sigmund Jähn (Intercosmos), first German in space — Soyuz 31/29 (1978) (flew for East Germany)  
*   Ulf Merbold, EAC — STS-9 (1983), STS-42 (1992), Soyuz TM-20/19 (1994) (flew for both West Germany and united Germany)  
*   Ernst Messerschmid — STS-61-A (1985) (flew for West Germany)  
*   Reinhard Furrer, born in Wörgl, Austria (1940–1995) — STS-61-A (1985) (flew for West Germany)  
*   Klaus-Dietrich Flade — Soyuz TM-14/13 (1992)  
*   Ulrich Walter — STS-55 (1993)  
*   Hans Schlegel, EAC — STS-55 (1993), STS-122 (2008)  
*   Reinhold Ewald, EAC — Soyuz TM-25/24 (1997)  
*   Gerhard Thiele, EAC — STS-99 (2000)  
*   Thomas Reiter, EAC, first German to walk in space and first ESA astronaut to stay on the ISS. — Soyuz TM-22 (1995), STS-121/116 (2006)  
*   Alexander Gerst, EAC — Soyuz TMA-13M (2014), Soyuz MS-09 (2018)  
*   Matthias Maurer, EAC — SpaceX Crew-3 (2021)  
*   _Rabea Rogge_ — Fram2 (2025), first German woman in space

*   Bertalan Farkas (Intercosmos), first Hungarian in space. — Soyuz 36/35 (1980)  
*   Tibor Kapu, HUNOR — Axiom Mission 4 (2025)

## Orbital space travelers
### European Space Agency members
*   Franco Malerba, first Italian in space. — STS-46 (1992)  
*   Maurizio Cheli, EAC — STS-75 (1996)  
*   Umberto Guidoni, EAC — STS-75 (1996), STS-100 (2001)  
*   Roberto Vittori, EAC — Soyuz TM-34/33 (2002), Soyuz TMA-6/5 (2005), STS-134 (2011)  
*   Paolo A. Nespoli, EAC — STS-120 (2007), Soyuz TMA-20 (2010), Soyuz MS-05 (2017)  
*   Luca Parmitano, EAC, first Italian to walk in space.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_space_travelers_by_nationality#cite_note-8) — Soyuz TMA-09M (2013), Soyuz MS-13 (2019)  
*   Samantha Cristoforetti, EAC, first Italian woman in space — Soyuz TMA-15M (2014), SpaceX Crew-4 (2022)  
*   Walter Villadei — Axiom Mission 3 (2024)

*   Wubbo Ockels, EAC, first Dutchman in space. — STS-61-A (1985)  
*   André Kuipers, EAC — Soyuz TMA-4/3 (2004), Soyuz TMA-03M (2011)

*   _Jannicke Mikkelsen_, also holds British citizenship. — Fram2 (2025)
(Marcus Wandt, who went on Axiom Mission 3 in 2024, is listed under Sweden but also holds a Norwegian passport.)

Title: Jean-Loup Chrétien
Chunks: 0,1,2
Jean-Loup Chrétien (born August 20, 1938) is the first French astronaut to travel into space and was awarded the title Геро́й Сове́тского Сою́за.
On June 24, 1982, Chrétien, along with Union of Soviet Socialist Republics cosmonauts, docked with the Salyut 7 space station aboard the Soyuz T-6 spacecraft, carried out the Soviet-French joint experimental program, completing experiments such as the French ultrasonic cardiovascular monitoring system, accumulating a total flight time of 7 days, 21 hours, 50 minutes, and 42 seconds. On November 26, 1988, during the Soyuz TM-7 mission, he and Alexander Volkov performed a spacewalk lasting 5 hours and 57 minutes to install the French ERA experimental deployable structure, becoming the first non-American and non-Soviet astronaut to perform an extravehicular activity. This mission lasted 24 days, 18 hours, and 7 minutes. On September 25, 1997, he participated in the Space Shuttle Atlantis STS-86 mission, which accomplished the 7th docking between a Space Shuttle and the Mir space station, delivering an attitude control computer and retrieving experiment samples from STS-76. During this mission, he also participated in experiments on plant reproduction in a microgravity environment. The mission lasted 10 days, 19 hours, and 21 minutes.

. Chrétien was the first French astronaut to enter space. On 24 June 1982, Chrétien, Dzhanibekov, and Ivanchenkov were launched aboard Soyuz T-6 and docked with Salyut 7, joining the crew of Berezovoy and Lebedev already on the space station. They spent nearly seven days carrying out the Soviet-French joint experimental program, which included a series of experiments with the French ultrasonic cardiovascular monitoring system. The flight time was 7 days, 21 hours, 50 minutes, and 42 seconds.
1
On 26 November 1988, Chrétien was launched as a research astronaut with Volkov and Krikalev aboard Soyuz TM-7, which docked with the Mir space station. They spent 22 days completing the Soviet-French joint experimental program, which included a 5-hour 57-minute spacewalk by Volkov and Chrétien, during which they installed the French ERA experimental deployable structure and material sample panels. The mission lasted 24 days 18 hours 7 minutes.
1
From September 25 to October 6, 1997, he joined the crew of Space Shuttle Atlantis on mission STS-86, the seventh Shuttle-Mir docking mission. Highlights of this mission included the delivery of a Mir attitude control computer, the crew rotation of American astronauts Mike Foale and David Wolf, a spacewalk by Scott Parazynski and Vladimir Titov to retrieve experiment samples first deployed during the STS-76/Mir docking mission, the delivery of 10,400 pounds of scientific and logistical payload to Mir, and the return of experiment hardware and results to Earth. The mission duration was 10 days, 19 hours, and 21 minutes.
1
Honors and Awards
He was the first French astronaut and was awarded the title of Геро́й Сове́тского Сою́за in 1982 (French: Héros de l'Union soviétique).
1
Major Contributions
Chrétien became the first astronaut who was neither American nor Soviet to perform a spacewalk.
Participation in Design Projects

In 2009, Jean-Loup Chrétien participated in the design of the "Ocean Space Station", which resembled a spacecraft in appearance, and its anti-collision system technology was derived from similar designs used on the International Space Station.

## Orbital space travelers
### European Space Agency members
[edit]
Some of these astronauts participated in national space programme activity unrelated to their home country's contemporary or subsequent membership of the European Space Agency.
*   Franz Viehböck, first Austrian in space. — Soyuz TM-13/12 (1991)

*   Dirk Frimout, first Belgian in space. — STS-45 (1992)  
*   Frank De Winne, EAC — Soyuz TMA-1/TM-34 (2002), Soyuz TMA-15 (2009)

*   Andreas Mogensen, EAC, first Dane in space. — Soyuz TMA-18M (2015)/16M (2015), SpaceX Crew-7 (2023)

## Orbital space travelers
### European Space Agency members
*   Jean-Loup Chrétien, CNES (Intercosmos), first French person in space and first non-Soviet European to walk in space — Soyuz T-6 (1982), Soyuz TM-7/6 (1988), STS-86 (1997)  
*   Patrick Baudry, second Frenchman in space, born in Douala, Cameroon — STS-51-G (1985)  
*   Michel Tognini, EAC — Soyuz TM-15/14 (1992), STS-93 (1999)  
*   Jean-Pierre Haigneré, EAC — Soyuz TM-17/16 (1993), Soyuz TM-29 (1999)  
*   Jean-François Clervoy, EAC — STS-66 (1994), STS-84 (1997), STS-103 (1999)  
*   Jean-Jacques Favier, born in Kehl, Germany — STS-78 (1996)  
*   Claudie André-Deshays Haigneré, EAC, first Frenchwoman in space (Mir, 1996) — Soyuz TM-24/23 (1996), Soyuz TM-33/32 (2001)  
*   Léopold Eyharts, EAC — Soyuz TM-27/26 (1998), STS-122/123 (2008)  
*   Philippe Perrin, EAC, born in Meknes, Morocco — STS-111 (2002)  
*   Thomas Pesquet, EAC — Soyuz MS-03 (2016), SpaceX Crew-2 (2021)  
*   Sophie Adenot, EAC — SpaceX Crew-12 (2026)

## Orbital space travelers
### European Space Agency members
*   Sigmund Jähn (Intercosmos), first German in space — Soyuz 31/29 (1978) (flew for East Germany)  
*   Ulf Merbold, EAC — STS-9 (1983), STS-42 (1992), Soyuz TM-20/19 (1994) (flew for both West Germany and united Germany)  
*   Ernst Messerschmid — STS-61-A (1985) (flew for West Germany)  
*   Reinhard Furrer, born in Wörgl, Austria (1940–1995) — STS-61-A (1985) (flew for West Germany)  
*   Klaus-Dietrich Flade — Soyuz TM-14/13 (1992)  
*   Ulrich Walter — STS-55 (1993)  
*   Hans Schlegel, EAC — STS-55 (1993), STS-122 (2008)  
*   Reinhold Ewald, EAC — Soyuz TM-25/24 (1997)  
*   Gerhard Thiele, EAC — STS-99 (2000)  
*   Thomas Reiter, EAC, first German to walk in space and first ESA astronaut to stay on the ISS. — Soyuz TM-22 (1995), STS-121/116 (2006)  
*   Alexander Gerst, EAC — Soyuz TMA-13M (2014), Soyuz MS-09 (2018)  
*   Matthias Maurer, EAC — SpaceX Crew-3 (2021)  
*   _Rabea Rogge_ — Fram2 (2025), first German woman in space

*   Bertalan Farkas (Intercosmos), first Hungarian in space. — Soyuz 36/35 (1980)  
*   Tibor Kapu, HUNOR — Axiom Mission 4 (2025)

## Orbital space travelers
### European Space Agency members
*   Franco Malerba, first Italian in space. — STS-46 (1992)  
*   Maurizio Cheli, EAC — STS-75 (1996)  
*   Umberto Guidoni, EAC — STS-75 (1996), STS-100 (2001)  
*   Roberto Vittori, EAC — Soyuz TM-34/33 (2002), Soyuz TMA-6/5 (2005), STS-134 (2011)  
*   Paolo A. Nespoli, EAC — STS-120 (2007), Soyuz TMA-20 (2010), Soyuz MS-05 (2017)  
*   Luca Parmitano, EAC, first Italian to walk in space.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_space_travelers_by_nationality#cite_note-8) — Soyuz TMA-09M (2013), Soyuz MS-13 (2019)  
*   Samantha Cristoforetti, EAC, first Italian woman in space — Soyuz TMA-15M (2014), SpaceX Crew-4 (2022)  
*   Walter Villadei — Axiom Mission 3 (2024)

*   Wubbo Ockels, EAC, first Dutchman in space. — STS-61-A (1985)  
*   André Kuipers, EAC — Soyuz TMA-4/3 (2004), Soyuz TMA-03M (2011)

*   _Jannicke Mikkelsen_, also holds British citizenship. — Fram2 (2025)
(Marcus Wandt, who went on Axiom Mission 3 in 2024, is listed under Sweden but also holds a Norwegian passport.)

Jean-Loup Chrétien (born August 20, 1938) is the first French astronaut to travel into space and was awarded the title Геро́й Сове́тского Сою́за.
On June 24, 1982, Chrétien, along with Union of Soviet Socialist Republics cosmonauts, docked with the Salyut 7 space station aboard the Soyuz T-6 spacecraft, carried out the Soviet-French joint experimental program, completing experiments such as the French ultrasonic cardiovascular monitoring system, accumulating a total flight time of 7 days, 21 hours, 50 minutes, and 42 seconds. On November 26, 1988, during the Soyuz TM-7 mission, he and Alexander Volkov performed a spacewalk lasting 5 hours and 57 minutes to install the French ERA experimental deployable structure, becoming the first non-American and non-Soviet astronaut to perform an extravehicular activity. This mission lasted 24 days, 18 hours, and 7 minutes. On September 25, 1997, he participated in the Space Shuttle Atlantis STS-86 mission, which accomplished the 7th docking between a Space Shuttle and the Mir space station, delivering an attitude control computer and retrieving experiment samples from STS-76. During this mission, he also participated in experiments on plant reproduction in a microgravity environment. The mission lasted 10 days, 19 hours, and 21 minutes.

France
Taikonaut

. Chrétien was the first French astronaut to enter space. On 24 June 1982, Chrétien, Dzhanibekov, and Ivanchenkov were launched aboard Soyuz T-6 and docked with Salyut 7, joining the crew of Berezovoy and Lebedev already on the space station. They spent nearly seven days carrying out the Soviet-French joint experimental program, which included a series of experiments with the French ultrasonic cardiovascular monitoring system. The flight time was 7 days, 21 hours, 50 minutes, and 42 seconds.
1
On 26 November 1988, Chrétien was launched as a research astronaut with Volkov and Krikalev aboard Soyuz TM-7, which docked with the Mir space station. They spent 22 days completing the Soviet-French joint experimental program, which included a 5-hour 57-minute spacewalk by Volkov and Chrétien, during which they installed the French ERA experimental deployable structure and material sample panels. The mission lasted 24 days 18 hours 7 minutes.
1
From September 25 to October 6, 1997, he joined the crew of Space Shuttle Atlantis on mission STS-86, the seventh Shuttle-Mir docking mission. Highlights of this mission included the delivery of a Mir attitude control computer, the crew rotation of American astronauts Mike Foale and David Wolf, a spacewalk by Scott Parazynski and Vladimir Titov to retrieve experiment samples first deployed during the STS-76/Mir docking mission, the delivery of 10,400 pounds of scientific and logistical payload to Mir, and the return of experiment hardware and results to Earth. The mission duration was 10 days, 19 hours, and 21 minutes.
1

Chrétien became the first astronaut who was neither American nor Soviet to perform a spacewalk.
